# `Q-3-43` — Generated content edit dropped

> An edit typed into pipeline-generated content was reverted; the
> content has no editable source position in this file.

## What this means

This warning comes from the visual editor in `q2 preview` and Quarto
Hub, not from a command-line render.

Parts of a rendered document are produced by Quarto rather than typed
by you. A resolved cross-reference is the clearest example: you write
`@fig-plot`, and the editor shows **Figure 3**. Those characters are
generated — the number depends on how many figures precede it, and no
part of the phrase exists in your `.qmd`.

The editor treats such regions as single atomic units. You can replace
or delete one wholesale, but you cannot type inside it, because there
are no source bytes to write the keystrokes back to. An edit that
lands inside is reverted.

Your document is unchanged.

## Why this happens

- **Typing inside a resolved cross-reference.** Clicking into
  "Figure 3" and editing the number or the word.
- **A selection spanning generated content**, then typing over it.
- **Editing content that came from elsewhere** — an included file, a
  metadata value — which has a source, just not in the file you have
  open.

## How to fix

Edit the upstream source that produced the content.

For a cross-reference, change the referenced element's label or its
position in the document; the number is computed from document order
and is not editable directly:

```markdown
![A scatter plot](plot.png){#fig-plot}

As @fig-plot shows, ...
```

For content from an include, open the included file and edit it there.
For content from metadata, edit the metadata key in the front matter or
`_quarto.yml`.

To remove generated content entirely, delete the whole unit rather than
editing within it — deletion of an atomic region is supported.
